title: Release notes: add style linter + block internal-only fields (CI enforcement)
author: Wei Chen
description: This PR adds a release-notes style linter for model changelog templates/content and enforces it in CI. Motivation: as we wire the model changelog generator into the docs site, we need a hard guardrail to prevent accidental publication of internal-only metadata (internal model nicknames, vendor details, routing policy IDs, etc.) and to keep customer-visible notes consistent across models/teams. What’s included: (1) a small linter that validates frontmatter keys against an allowlist and scans content for prohibited tokens/phrasing, (2) validation that required sections are present (Impact, Compatibility, Links; Deprecation when applicable), (3) consistent formatting rules (heading levels, date format, link targets), and (4) a GitHub Actions job that runs on PRs touching release notes templates or generated release note content. This is intended to be a fast, deterministic check (no network calls) and to fail with actionable errors. Notes: the allowlist aligns with the Model Metadata Schema v1 public fields and is intentionally stricter than what the internal registry stores; if we need to add a new customer-visible field, we should update the allowlist + style guide together. Follow-ups: once the generator output stabilizes, we can add fixtures from staging feeds to catch regressions in templating output formatting. Screenshots: N/A (CI-only change).

conversation: Elliot Price (review): Nice. Two requests: (1) please ensure the linter error output points to the exact field/token that triggered the failure (not just 'internal field found'), and (2) make 'Known limitations' optional but recommended (don’t fail if missing).

Wei Chen (author): Updated output formatting to include file:line and the specific prohibited key/token. Also changed Known limitations to a warning (non-blocking) and kept Impact/Compatibility/Links as required.

Kira Thompson (review): Can we explicitly block the internal frontmatter keys we’ve seen in drafts (internal_model_name, provider, vendor_contract_id, routing_policy_id) even if they’re not in allowlist? Helps with clearer error messages vs. generic allowlist failure. Also, please add a note in README about how to request allowlist changes (PM sign-off).

Wei Chen (author): Added explicit denylist with custom messages for the keys listed + a couple more (internal_notes, release_manager). Added README section: 'Requesting new public fields' with PM-801 reference and docs style guide link.

Monica Patel (review): One minor thing: compatibility section should mention API surface changes (tool calling / structured output) explicitly when present, but shouldn’t force the words 'tool calling' for every note. Can we make it a template hint rather than lint rule?
Wei Chen (author): Agreed—kept it as guidance in README and not a lint requirement. Lint only asserts that Compatibility exists and is non-empty.
Elliot Price (approve): Approved. This will save us from re-litigating wording and accidental leakage later. Please merge after CI green.
Wei Chen (author): CI green; squashing and merging.
release_notes: Internal-only (docs tooling): adds CI enforcement to prevent internal metadata leakage in customer-visible model release notes and standardizes required sections/formatting.
